checks: The affine majorant is positive on the entire compact interval because it majorizes the positive profile. At s=0 the section lies at z=0 and integration in x gives C(0)=r_0^m and M(0)=0.

For s>0 the raw coarea in the z-coordinate is r^(m−1) dz/(2s) on |z|≤sr(z). The change q=z/[s(1+b_0 z)] has the claimed Jacobian and sends that set into [−r_0,r_0]. Combining the affine upper bound on r with d=m+1 gives complete cancellation of the denominator powers. This also covers m=1.

The tangent inequality is (1+b_0 z)^−d≥1−d b_0 z. When b_0≠0 it is strict for z≠0, and each positive finite slope has positive density on an interval around zero. Hence each such slope gives a strictly smaller value of C−d b_0M than C(0).

The weighted bound and the uniform positive lower and finite upper bounds on the denominator give bounded coarea and moment for all slopes. Averaging is valid for every probability law on finite slopes, and zero average moment removes the linear term. Strictness then forces full mass at s=0, which attains equality.

Compared candidate 5b3b585d1663ccd0 §6, (7)–(9) and its strictness argument. Independently evaluated the raw and projectively weighted section integrals for r(z)=1+z/2 on [−1,1] at slopes 1/3, 2/3, 1, 2 and 4 by exact fractions.

overlap.comparison: Gives a nonnegative coarea defect from a lower affine support of the reciprocal profile under individual section centering. The present inequality uses an upper support of the original radius and applies to every slope and to zero-moment mixtures without individual centering.
Gives centered energy bounds for a specified affine cone. Those formulas do not give this tangent-majorant estimate for arbitrary positive concave profiles.

readability: Strictness for a mixture with positive mass away from zero needs no uniform strict gap at small positive slopes.

summary: The supporting affine majorant gives the stated projectively weighted coarea bound and the sharp equality condition for zero-moment mixtures when its slope is nonzero.
